headline: High: Flowise and n8n both write shared server-side state, broad egress, and unverified handoff paths create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write server filesystem and uses graph-based tool flows; n8n can also read/write server filesystem and orchestrate tools as workflow nodes. A shared filesystem or datastore handoff can let attacker-controlled content from one agent be treated as instructions by the other, though no direct clipboard/MCP bridge is shown.
conditions: IF Flowise writes untrusted content into a shared file or datastore that n8n later parses as workflow instructions
IF n8n ingests Flowise-generated text without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents onto distinct workspaces
Add provenance tags to all exchanged files
Disable automatic parsing of shared text as instructions
Review any file-based handoff before execution

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise handles model provider keys and tool credentials, while n8n stores per-credential secrets and can call many integration nodes. Both have broad network egress and filesystem access, so a shared workspace or connected system can expose secrets or workflow data to the other and onward to third parties.
conditions: IF either agent stores secrets or sensitive workflow data in a shared filesystem
IF n8n integration nodes transmit Flowise-produced files or context to external services
mitigations: Store secrets in separate credential stores
Restrict shared folders to non-sensitive artifacts
Turn off automatic file uploads in workflows
Rotate any credentials exposed in shared outputs
requires-engineering: add per-agent data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the server filesystem and run concurrently with shared state via server datastore or connected systems. That creates a direct write-write conflict surface, and n8n additionally has Execute Command on the server, increasing the chance of clobbering or racing Flowise-managed files.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or datastore without locking
IF n8n Execute Command modifies files that Flowise also writes
mitigations: Assign disjoint write directories
Enable file locks or transactional writes
Disable Execute Command for shared paths
Serialize jobs touching the same datastore
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise produces graph-based outputs and tool calls that n8n can consume as workflow inputs. Because n8n can execute commands and invoke many integrations, treating Flowise output as authoritative can turn a mistaken or injected output into real downstream actions without a verification step.
conditions: IF n8n uses Flowise output directly as an action payload
IF no human or schema verification occurs between Flowise generation and n8n execution
mitigations: Insert a validation step before execution
Require human approval for destructive actions
Constrain n8n to read-only test workflows
Use schema checks on Flowise outputs
requires-engineering: add signed handoff contracts

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, but Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs while n8n processes whatever the workflow handles. If regulated data enters both, differing retention, logging, or residency settings across the two systems can create a compliance mismatch; the profiles do not prove a specific violation, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through both systems
IF their logging or retention settings differ for the same data class
mitigations: Document data classes per workflow
Align retention settings across both systems
Disable verbose logs for sensitive runs
Review residency settings before deployment
requires-engineering: implement policy enforcement across both stacks
